contradictions.what: Rep says lost on price and 'we win this' with rate room, but also admits IT's spring timing worry and that the page would still say same rate, 'maybe not only the rate'.
Rep says nothing got silence and it was a good cycle, yet Lucy asked for a business case for Martin and got only the generic deck.
Rep says the price comparison was unfair and 'the same thing' is wrong, yet we supplied no total-cost or value figure to counter it.
Rep says Lucy was sold and no figure was needed, but then admits Martin had nothing from us on what the failures cost.
Lucy called it a formality right before the CFO meeting; the real decider was never engaged by us.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Answered 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed,' giving no silent part, and moved to 'We lost on price.'

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide and 'Lucy got it'; only admitted no Fernbrook figure when pressed at T32.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Paused, said 'Nothing from us,' then assumed Lucy told him.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Mentioned the one-page business case request only as 'once' and framed sending the deck as an answer.
